verdict.rationale: Better Auth's session-management docs cover configurable expiry (expiresIn, default 7 days) and sliding refresh via updateAge, including a POST-based refresh flow. Revocation is documented only as a logged-in user revoking their own sessions on other devices. Nothing shows an immediate server-side or admin-initiated kill of a specific compromised session, or that revocation takes effect right away. Missing for 10: documented server-side/admin revocation of a specific compromised session, evidence that revocation is immediate (e.g. under cookie or JWT caching), independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage session lifecycle — expiry, refresh, and immediate server-side revocation of a compromised session

citations.quote: The session expires after 7 days by default. But whenever the session is used and the updateAge is reached, the session expiration is updated
You can change both the `expiresIn` and `updateAge` values by passing the `session` object to the `auth` configuration.
The client automatically calls POST to perform the refresh.
A logged in user can also revoke their own sessions to log out from different devices or browsers.
